jack.how: a boy of five to ten: quick, a little sulky, shy of grown-ups; hides feelings behind short words; when he speaks Mandarin Chinese, a child's plain home Chinese, natural

jack_grown.how: a young man of twenty-one, quiet and tired, says little and keeps it plain; tender only in what he does, never in big words; when he speaks Mandarin Chinese, a little rusty, plain home Chinese

mom.how: a Chinese woman in her thirties and forties, small and gentle, light and quietly cheerful, hiding her weight under a joke; in Mandarin Chinese a native speaker, warm, quick and natural, a village accent; in English slow and careful, with a Chinese accent, choosing every word

dad.how: an American father in his forties and fifties: kind, awkward, a once-stammering man; rambles a little about small things, very short about what matters; never raises his voice

mark.how: an American boy of ten from across the street: loud, quick, hurt and showing off, repeating what grown-ups say

mark_grown.how: an American man of twenty-two, easy-going on the surface, a little awkward

kids.how: a couple of boys of ten at a school bus stop, jeering together, laughing

nurse.how: a hospital nurse in her fifties, tired and warm, kind without fuss; says hard things gently, as she does every day

translator.how: a Chinese woman of about fifty-five from a tour group, from the north of China, in a hurry: quick, talkative, practical; reading aloud she slows down despite herself and is moved; in Mandarin Chinese a native northern speaker; in other languages fluent with a light Chinese accent

guide.how: a tour guide calling across a square, loud and cheerful
